description: Two resonators, which are band pass filters that can be made to peak very narrowly.

params.text: Switches between the two resonators: ResonA, a plain conjugate pole pair, and ResonB, the Smith-Angell design with a more symmetrical response.
Sets the corner frequency of the filter, 20Hz to 20480Hz, starting at 261.63Hz.
Attenuates the cutoff CV input, and inverts it when turned below zero.
Sets the -3dB bandwidth of the resonator, marked as a Q of 0.707 to 20.
Attenuates the quality CV input, and inverts it when turned below zero.
Sets how much of the unfiltered input is mixed into the outputs, 0 to 100%, starting at nothing.
Sets how much of the filtered signal reaches the outputs, 0 to 100%, starting at 100%.

inputs.text: The audio to be filtered; sixteen channels are filtered separately.
Shifts the corner frequency by one octave per volt, scaled by its attenuverter.
Raises the quality factor Q; 10V adds the whole range of 20 with its attenuverter at maximum.

outputs.text: The resonator output, clamped between -5V and 5V.

notes: the cutoff and quality CV inputs are each multiplied by the attenuverter beside them, and those start at zero, so a patched cable changes nothing until one is turned up.
menu: Structure — chooses the arithmetic the biquad is calculated with: Direct, Canonical, TransposeDirect or TransposeCanonical, the last of which stays steadiest under fast modulation.
